description: I’m a third-year Computer Science Engineering student interested in AI/ML, web development, and space exploration. I’m building AstroBase, an interactive mission trainer that helps children understand life on the Moon or Mars through fun challenges. I’m looking for enthusiastic teammates interested in React, JavaScript, UI/UX design, game development, data visualization, or space science. Beginners willing to learn, collaborate, and share ideas are welcome! 🚀
summary:
AstroBase — Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer is an interactive educational space mission simulator designed to help students aged 7–12 explore the challenges of living and working on the Moon and Mars.

The project allows learners to select a planetary outpost, respond to five simulated mission events, and make decisions while managing three essential resources: power, life support, and radiation protection. Each decision can affect the simulated condition of the outpost, helping learners understand the trade-offs involved in space exploration.

Through interactive scenarios, mission feedback, and scientific explanations, AstroBase introduces concepts such as solar storms, energy conservation, environmental control, life-support systems, and planetary exploration. The project draws on NASA space science and exploration resources to connect interactive learning with real scientific concepts.

AstroBase aims to make space science more engaging and accessible by encouraging curiosity, critical thinking, decision-making, and STEM learning through a hands-on mission experience.
details:
AstroBase — Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer

Project Overview

AstroBase is an interactive educational web application designed to introduce students aged 7–12 to the challenges of space exploration. It allows learners to experience simulated missions at lunar and Martian outposts while learning about planetary environments, astronaut safety, resource management, and scientific decision-making.

How It Works

Learners explore two simulated outposts: Artemis Outpost Alpha on the Moon and Ares Pioneer Hab 1 on Mars. During a mission, they encounter different scenarios, such as a solar storm warning, a low-power emergency, life-support maintenance, a scientific research opportunity, and a communication failure.

Players choose how to respond to each situation and observe how their decisions affect three simulated resources: Power Grid, Life Support, and Radiation Protection. Feedback explains the consequences of decisions and connects them to scientific concepts relevant to space exploration.

Benefits and Intended Impact

AstroBase makes space science more engaging through interactive, scenario-based learning. It encourages curiosity, critical thinking, problem-solving, and an understanding of how astronauts must balance safety, energy, and life-support needs in challenging environments.

The project is intended to support STEM education by making complex space exploration concepts easier for younger learners to understand.

NASA Resources and Scientific Inspiration

The project draws on NASA's space science and exploration resources to inform its educational scenarios and scientific explanations. The Moon and Mars settings introduce learners to the different challenges of exploring these environments.

The mission scenarios and resource indicators are educational simulations. Their values are illustrative and should not be interpreted as real spacecraft telemetry, validated engineering calculations, or operational guidance.

Technology

AstroBase was developed as a web-based application using the technologies implemented in the project, including React, Vite, JavaScript, JSX, and CSS. The application is designed to provide an interactive and accessible learning experience through a web browser.

Creativity and Design Considerations

The project combines mission-based storytelling, interactive decisions, resource indicators, and explanatory feedback in one learning experience. Its design considers the intended age group, ease of use, educational value, and the importance of communicating scientific concepts clearly.

AstroBase is an independent educational project created for the NASA Space Apps Challenge. It is not an official NASA product and is not endorsed by NASA.
